title: Hidden Gems in Motovun, Croatia: Local Spots 2027
metaDescription: Off-the-beaten-path Motovun: Parenzana trail, forest walks, Livade truffle hunts at €15, village restaurants and quiet hilltop neighbours. Prices and tips.
content:
## What Most Visitors Skip in Motovun

Motovun sits on a 277 m hill, and nearly every visitor stays on top of it. The less-visited part is the valley floor: oak forest, a disused railway line, small truffle farms and village restaurants where prices are lower than inside the walls. The hilltop sights are covered elsewhere. This guide stays below them.

## Motovun Forest on Foot

The Motovun Forest is a protected floodplain oak woodland along the Mirna River. It is a rare wet forest in otherwise dry Istrian karst, and it is one of the best-known habitats of the white truffle (Tuber magnatum). Most people only look at it from the town walls. Walking in it is free, but the ground is damp, so wear boots even in summer. Do not dig anywhere: truffle collecting is regulated and licensed.

## Livade: The Valley Village With the Cheaper Truffle Meals

Livade, in the valley below Motovun, is where the truffle trade actually happens. It is the base for the Zigante family, who found the 1,310 g white truffle in 1999, and for several independent hunters.

- **Group hunt:** Zigante runs a group hunt every Saturday at the Livade 7 shop and restaurant, from the first Saturday of June to the last Saturday of September. It costs €15 per person, children under 10 are free, and it lasts about an hour. Check the start time (listed as 17:00 on the operator's page, with some guides showing 19:00) when you book.
- **Private hunt:** Private hunts run all year by request and start at €150 for up to five people. Karlić Tartufi, a family farm in Paladini near Buzet, also offers private hunts with a tasting and a truffle museum stop.
- **Meeting point for independent guides:** One guided walk starts near the Parenzana museum in Livade, at a wooden house on the large car park.

**Opinion:** Skip the €100+ per person truffle "experience" packages sold inside the old town. The €15 Saturday group hunt in Livade uses the same forest and dogs, and the saved money buys a full truffle lunch.

At the village gostionica level, a meal with two large soups, two white truffle dishes and a bottle of local wine has been reported at around €55–60 for two people, noticeably less than hilltop restaurants. Prices vary by season, so confirm before ordering truffles, which are usually charged by weight.

## Parenzana Trail: The Old Railway Line

The Parenzana was a narrow-gauge railway that ran through Istria in the early 20th century. Its route is now a walking and cycling path. Near Motovun it follows the valley with gentle gradients, so it suits casual cyclists better than the hill roads. A practical plan is to cycle the flat valley section, then continue to quieter hill villages such as Grožnjan or Oprtalj. Bring water, because shade and shops are scarce between villages.

## Seasonal Timing

- **Black summer truffle:** April to late September.
- **White truffle:** September into January, with the peak and highest prices from October to December.
- **Zigante Truffle Days:** an annual truffle fair in Livade, held on weekends from early October to early November. It is busy, so go early on a weekday for the forest and valley instead.
- **Quietest months:** spring and winter, when the hill town is calm and valley mornings are often misty.

## Insider Tips

- Stay or park in the valley and walk or cycle up. Cars cannot enter the old town centre freely, and parking at the top fills by midday in summer.
- Buy truffle products at family farm shops. A fresh summer black truffle was priced around €50 per 100 g at one farm shop in 2026, and truffle spreads cost a few euros per jar.
- Book hunts in advance for weekends in October.
- Learn to read labels: truffle oil is often flavoured, not made with real truffle.

## Getting There

Motovun is about 35 km inland from Poreč. A car is the simplest option for reaching Livade, farm shops and neighbouring hill villages, while the valley section of the Parenzana suits bicycles.

faq.question: What are the best hidden gems in Motovun?
faq.answer: The best lesser-known spots are the Motovun Forest, the Parenzana railway trail, and the valley village of Livade with its truffle hunts and cheaper restaurants. Quiet hill villages such as Grožnjan and Oprtalj are also easy to reach from the trail.

faq.question: How much does a truffle hunt near Motovun cost?
faq.answer: A Zigante group hunt in Livade costs €15 per person, with children under 10 free, and runs on Saturdays from June to September. Private hunts start at €150 for up to five people, and some farms only give prices on request.

faq.question: When is truffle season in Motovun?
faq.answer: Black summer truffles are found from April to late September. White truffles are in season from September into January, with October to December being the busiest and most expensive period.

faq.question: Can you walk or cycle around Motovun without a tour?
faq.answer: Yes. The Motovun Forest and the Parenzana trail are free to use without a guide. Wear waterproof footwear in the forest and do not dig for truffles, as collecting is regulated.

quickAnswer: Motovun's best hidden spots are below the hilltop: the Motovun Forest floodplain, the Parenzana railway trail, the village of Livade with its €15 group truffle hunts and cheaper truffle restaurants, and quiet neighbouring hill villages. Go early or on weekdays, and use the valley rather than the old town as your base.
